T01_design_usage_model.title: Design the usage data model, metrics and UI layout
T01_design_usage_model.instruction:
Goal: fix the design every later node builds on. Write a '## Usage' section in docs/DESIGN.md and the shared types in src/shared/usage.ts (types and constants only, no logic).

Findings already gathered (verify, don't re-derive from scratch):
- Session JSONL (version 3): header {type:'session', id, cwd, timestamp}; model_change, thinking_level_change, session_info {name}, compaction, context_edit, custom {customType: subagents:record, pi-context-gc-checkpoint, web-search-results, ...}, custom_message; message with role system | user | assistant | toolResult. Entries form a tree (id/parentId); abandoned branches still cost tokens, so count every entry in the file, not just the active branch.
- assistant message: provider, model, api, stopReason (toolUse | stop | error | aborted), errorMessage, thinkingLevel, timestamp (ms), usage {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, reasoning, cost{...,total}}, content blocks including toolCall {id, name}. toolResult: toolCallId, toolName, isError, timestamp, sometimes nestedCalls (codemode).
- claude-bridge is ~92% of assistant turns and records cost 0 (subscription via Claude Code); openai-codex records a cost. In the last two weeks claude-opus-5-5 alone had 29.3M output, 6.32B cache read, 137.7M cache write and only 72k uncached input tokens, about $2.5k at list price, roughly half of it cache reads. Cache tokens must be first-class everywhere.
- Source mix of files since 2026-09-26: 478 CI runner sessions (cwd under actions-runner folders), 157 card worktrees (cwd ~/.pi-gna/worktrees/<id>/<original absolute path>), 442 other sessions, 312 of them with pi-gna's tools (kanban_*, threads_*, pigna-visual-prompt.md) in the system message.
- Volume: up to ~7.5k assistant messages a day; tools led by bash (33k calls, 1,185 errors), read, grep, write, codemode, kanban_*, subagent, browser_*, computer_*; 152 compactions, 163 error and 101 aborted stops.

How others do it (adopt the good parts):
- ccusage: daily/weekly/monthly/session reports, 5-hour billing windows with burn rate, per-model breakdown, cache create/read shown separately, offline pricing, recorded-vs-calculated cost modes; it already reads pi sessions and calculates cost when pi recorded 0.
- Claude Code /usage: cost computed locally at list price and labelled an estimate; activity stats; attribution to subagents, skills, MCP servers; flags behaviours over 10% of usage (long context, cache misses) with a tip each.
- Sniffly: error breakdown by category, interruption rate, tools and steps per prompt, cache analysis, hourly pattern, per-project cost split.

Decide and document:
1. Sources and classification: which roots are scanned; surface per session (pi-gna chat, card worktree, ATP worker/orchestrator, subagent, CI runner, terminal pi) and how each is detected; how worktree paths fold back to their project. Check where subagent sessions are written and whether their usage can be attributed to the parent.
2. Dedupe: whether forked/copied sessions repeat entries (check the header for a parent-session field and look for duplicated entry ids across files) and the dedupe key.
3. Per-file facts (FileUsageFacts): compact enough to cache for thousands of files. Suggested: UTC hour buckets keyed by provider+model holding token counts by type, recorded cost and turn count; tool stats (calls, errors, duration sum and count, measured from the assistant message to its toolResult); stop reasons; compactions; a context-size histogram (input+cacheRead+cacheWrite per turn); per-prompt stats (steps, tool calls, wall time, aborted); thinking levels; session meta (id, cwd, title or name, first and last timestamps, active time with idle gaps capped).
4. Cost model: 'API-equivalent estimate' at list price, kept separate from 'recorded cost'. Prices come from pi's installed pi-ai provider data (see T03), with an alias from claude-bridge to anthropic, tiered pricing, and an 'unpriced' bucket. Note: claude-haiku-5-5 is missing from that data.
5. Report API: host method `usage.get` {range (7d/14d/30d/90d/all or from/to), source filter (pi-gna only | all pi), project?} returning UsageReport, plus a `usage.progress` event while indexing. Bucket by local time at query time.
6. Metric list and wireframe of the section: headline stats; activity (daily stacked bars by model, tokens/cost toggle); calendar heatmap; weekday x hour heatmap; models table; projects; top sessions (open the chat); surfaces; tools; agent health; busiest 5-hour windows; behaviour insights with tips. Mark anything you consider out of scope.
7. Performance budget: cold index of the real data off the main thread, warm open under 500 ms, cache file size target.

Deliverables: the docs/DESIGN.md '## Usage' section; src/shared/usage.ts with FileUsageFacts, UsageQuery, UsageReport and related types; Settings > Usage listed in DESIGN.md's Settings paragraph.
Acceptance: the types compile (`pnpm typecheck`); every later node (T02 to T18) can find its inputs in the doc; decisions cite the real-file checks you ran.
T01_design_usage_model.context: Project: a Usage dashboard in pi-gna's Settings (new section 'Usage', group pi-gna) with in-depth, local-only analytics of how pi and pi-gna were used: tokens by type, estimated cost, models, projects, pi-gna surfaces (chats, card worktrees, ATP workers, subagents), tools, activity over time, agent health and behaviour insights. Data comes only from pi's session JSONL files on this Mac: sessionsDir() in src/main/session-index.ts (~/.pi/agent/sessions, ~1,100 files / 1.6 GB written in the last two weeks) plus pi-gna's userData/atp-sessions (~245 files / 142 MB). Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Principles (lean: no dependency on the pi package, no chart or component library, hand-written SVG + Tailwind; pi owns behaviour, so read pi's files; untrusted content), Settings, Remote access, Verifying the UI; and the '## Usage' section that T01 writes, which is the source of truth for types, metrics and file layout. Code style: flat files in src/main, src/shared, src/renderer/src/components, src/mobile with colocated *.test.ts (vitest); `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` must pass. Nothing leaves the machine: no network for pricing or anything else.
T01_design_usage_model.report:
## Outcome
DONE. The `## Usage` section is in `docs/DESIGN.md` (before `## Setup`), the shared shapes are in `src/shared/usage.ts`, and Settings > Usage is listed in the Settings paragraph. Commit `6604e55`. No external docs were used; every fact comes from pi's installed files and this Mac's session files, which I checked directly.

## Facts Learned
- Sessions: `sessions/<encoded cwd>/<ts>_<id>.jsonl` (1,428 files, 2.68 GB, 435 subagents in `<session>/tasks/`). ATP store: `userData/atp-sessions` (246 files, 142 MB). The two roots share no session id.
- Subagent headers carry `parentSession`; all 435 resolve to an existing parent file. The parent's `subagents:record` (456) has no usage, and its record id is not the child's session id.
- Header ids are unique. Eight-hex entry ids repeat across 6 unrelated pairs, so the dedupe key is `(session id, entry id)`. No forks or copies exist in the data.
- `totalTokens` = input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite on all 99,327 assistant turns. `reasoning` ≤ `output` on every turn (44,001 carry it).
- Tool durations (toolResult.timestamp − assistant.timestamp, ms): 114,625 timed calls, median 8.8 s, p90 33 s; bash median 9.3 s.
- Error messages cluster into categories (abort, rate limit "five_hour", overloaded/Service Unavailable, context window, SIGKILL process, WebSocket/timeout).
- claude-bridge records cost 0 (`pi-claude-bridge/src/models.ts:64`). Its `claude-haiku-5-5` is a local patch with zero cost; pi-ai's table has no haiku-5-5 (checked every bundle chunk).
- pi-ai's table lives in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/chunks/*.js` as `cost:{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite}` per million tokens. Tiers: only `inputTokensAbove: 272000` (openai-codex gpt-5.5 and gpt-6-astra). `calculateCost` applies the tier to the whole turn using input + cacheRead + cacheWrite.
- Surface markers: ATP worker = `### Runtime Context (Injected by pi-gna's ATP runner)` first message (246 ATP-store files); CI = cwd under `/actions-runners/`; card = `~/.pi-gna/worktrees/<6-char id>/`; pi-gna chat = system message names `kanban_`/`threads_`/`lament`/`pigna-visual-prompt` (434 of 1,076 sampled 14-day system messages name `kanban_`). The word `pi-gna` appears in 1,024 of 1,076 system messages, so it is not a marker (AGENTS.md mentions it).
- Shape cost, measured: 2,329 hour buckets, 1,457 provider/model keys, 4,567 tool-name entries across all 1,428 files, so the cache is about 1.5 MB. Cold scan of the 2.68 GB in Python (single thread, json per line) took 13.9 s.
- 14-day totals (1,322 files, all providers): 46,821 assistant turns, 7.58 billion cacheRead tokens.
- `projectOf(cwd)` in `src/shared/board.ts` already folds worktrees; reused.
- Baseline `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass before the change (node_modules was missing; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` fixed it).

## Decisions Made
- Two roots: `sessions` and `atp`, scanned recursively for `*.jsonl`.
- Surface precedence: subagent > atp-worker > ci > card > pigna-chat > terminal. `pigna` = pi-gna's surfaces plus subagents of a pigna parent.
- Project key = `projectOf(cwd)`; CI = `ci:<repo>` (segment after `/_work/`), so the runners form one project.
- Facts store tokens by hour bucket, never cost. Estimated cost is computed at query time from the price table, so price changes need no re-index. Tier-sensitive tokens are kept in `tierTokens` (turns above 272k).
- Recorded and estimated costs are separate fields, never summed.
- Cache-writes use the 5-minute rate (sessions have no 1-hour split); claude-bridge uses the `anthropic` table via `PRICE_PROVIDER_ALIASES`; unpriced turns are counted and shown.
- The price table is a vendored snapshot (T03), not read at runtime.
- Local time is applied at query time (`timeZone`, IANA); no local date is stored.
- `usage.get(query)` read-only, default `{range: "30d", source: "pigna"}`; `usage.progress` at most every 250 ms.
- Insight threshold 10% of base, max 6, by share. Five-hour blocks are hour-aligned from the first turn.
- Performance: cold index ≤ 30 s in a worker pool; warm `usage.get` ≤ 500 ms; cache ≤ 4 MB; lazy page chunk; no chart library.
- Out of scope for v1 (listed in the doc): budgets and alerts, CSV export, message content viewer, editing sessions, network rates, fast-mode/service-tier pricing, ATP orchestrator as its own surface, full phone charts.

## Files Touched
- `docs/DESIGN.md`: new `## Usage` section (lines ~1006–1231) with sub-sections Sources and surfaces, Dedupe and attribution, Per-file facts, Cost model, Report API, Metrics and layout, Performance budget, Verification, Inputs for later nodes (T02–T18 table), Open items and risks. The Settings paragraph now lists Usage in pi-gna, and a Settings bullet for Usage was added.
- `src/shared/usage.ts` (new): types and constants (see Interfaces Changed).
- `src/shared/usage.test.ts` (new): 3 tests locking the constant invariants (ascending edges, tier edge in CONTEXT_EDGES, version).

## Interfaces Changed
New shared module `src/shared/usage.ts` (types and constants only):
- Constants: `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` (1), `CONTEXT_TIER_EDGE` (272000), `ACTIVE_GAP_CAP_MS` (5 min), `CONTEXT_EDGES`, `STEP_EDGES`, `CACHE_MISS_MIN_INPUT` (10000), `SOURCE_ROOTS`, `SURFACES`, `STOP_REASONS`, `ERROR_CATEGORIES`, `INSIGHT_IDS`, `USAGE_RANGES`, `PRICE_PROVIDER_ALIASES`.
- Types: `SourceRoot`, `Surface`, `StopReason`, `ErrorCategory`, `InsightId`, `UsageRange`, `UsageSource` (`"pigna" | "all"`), `TokenCounts`, `UsageBucket`, `ToolStat`, `PromptStats`, `SessionMeta`, `FileUsageFacts`, `ModelRates`, `PriceEntry`, `PriceTable`, `UsageQuery`, `CostTotals`, `UsageTotals`, `UsageDay`, `WeekHour`, `ModelRow`, `ProjectRow`, `SessionRow`, `SurfaceRow`, `ToolRow`, `AgentHealth`, `WindowRow`, `Insight`, `UsageReportMeta`, `UsageReport`, `UsageProgress`.
- Not yet defined, owned by later nodes: `buildReport` signature (T06), the host method in `host-api.ts` (T08), the price lookup (T03).

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0, before and after the change.
- `pnpm test`: 157 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,454 tests passed, 3 skipped (includes `usage.test.ts`, 3/3 passing when run alone).
- Real-file checks, scripts run from the shell (one-off, not committed): the header and entry survey over all 1,428 session files plus the 246 ATP files; the duplicate-id and parentSession checks; the `totalTokens` identity; the error-message and tool-duration survey; the 14-day shape and surface-marker counts; the pi-ai table and haiku-5-5 grep; the cache-size estimate.
- Not run: no app or UI check (T01 is design only).

## Risks
- Surface heuristics: a pi-gna chat with every pi-gna feature off has no marker and counts as terminal. The ATP orchestrator's first message is not verified (T04 must check).
- Tool durations are upper bounds for parallel calls.
- The cache-write rate and the no-edge-change assumption for tiers are unverified against pi-ai's `calculateCost` beyond the one edge.
- claude-haiku-5-5 is unpriced until pi-ai lists it. A user-visible gap, by design.
- `pi-openai-fast-mode` may change billing; not modelled.
- The insight thresholds and tips are first guesses; T09 and T17 check them against the data.

## Recommended Next Step
T02 (per-file extractor) and T03 (price snapshot) can start in parallel from this section. Start with the types in `src/shared/usage.ts`; the per-field rules are under `## Usage` > Per-file facts and Cost model. T04 must settle the ATP orchestrator marker before T05 relies on surfaces.

T02_extract_session_facts.title: Implement the streaming per-file usage extractor
T02_extract_session_facts.instruction:
Goal: src/main/usage-extract.ts turns one session file into FileUsageFacts (types from src/shared/usage.ts, rules from DESIGN.md '## Usage').

Steps:
1. Stream the file line by line (reuse JsonlSplitter / safeParse patterns from src/main/session-file.ts and src/main/jsonl.ts). Parse only the lines that can matter: cheap substring checks before JSON.parse, since system messages and tool results are huge. Benchmark the gain.
2. Support incremental extraction: given previous facts and a byte offset, read only the appended bytes and merge (session files are append-only). Handle a partial trailing line.
3. Accumulate every metric T01 defined: hour buckets per provider+model, tool durations via toolCallId, per-prompt stats, stop reasons, compactions, context-size histogram, thinking levels, session meta and active time.
4. Tolerate bad lines and unknown entry types (count them, never throw).

Tests (src/main/usage-extract.test.ts) with small synthetic JSONL fixtures: a tool round trip, parallel tool calls, an error and an aborted stop, compaction, a branch (abandoned entries still counted), incremental append equals a full read, a truncated last line.
Acceptance: tests pass; on the largest real session file, extraction time and memory are recorded in the node report.

T02_extract_session_facts.report:
## Outcome
DONE. `src/main/usage-extract.ts` turns one session file into `FileUsageFacts`, streamed in byte chunks, with incremental resume from `consumedBytes`. Tests: 12 in `src/main/usage-extract.test.ts`. Commit `8048796`.

## Facts Learned
- `thinkingLevel` sits on assistant message objects (13,514 of 24,182 in a 400-file sample), not only on `thinking_level_change` entries. The per-level count uses the turn field.
- `nestedCalls` sits at the top level of the toolResult message (`nestedCalls.calls`), not in `details`. Codemode results carry it (43 in the sample).
- `subagents:record` is a top-level `custom` entry: `customType` at the top, `data.status` for the status.
- A toolResult's `toolCallId` equals the assistant `toolCall.id` exactly, including the `|fc_...` suffix.
- Bytes by record type over all 1,675 files (2.83 GB): toolResult 76%, assistant 15%, system messages 4.6%, user 2.7%.
- Totals over all 1,675 files: 99,375 assistant turns, 114,888 tool calls, 1,050 error turns, 1,675 sessions. The largest file (115.5 MB) matches a Python count exactly: 268 turns, 312 tool calls, 6 error turns, 10 prompts.

## Decisions Made
- Byte-level split instead of `JsonlSplitter`. The splitter works on strings and drops byte offsets, which resume needs. The LF and CR rules are the same.
- Substring prefilter on bytes: a record's type is read from its first key (`{"type":"..."`), and a message is parsed only when its role is user, assistant or toolResult. Skipped messages still tick the clock from their entry timestamp. Lines are decoded only when parsed.
- Resume: `consumedBytes` is the offset through the last complete record. A last line with no LF counts only once it parses. A file is resumed only when `size >= consumedBytes` and it already has a prompt; otherwise it is read in full.
- `prompts` in the facts is a derived view (closed prompts plus the open one). `resume.closed` holds the closed prompts; `resume.open` holds the open prompt; `resume.pending` holds unresolved tool calls.
- `wallMs` per prompt sums the capped gaps between its entries, from its user message on. A gap between the previous entry and a user message counts toward `activeMs` only.
- A failed turn is one with an `errorMessage`, or `stopReason` `error` or `aborted`. Its category is the first rule its message matches, else `aborted` for a `stopReason` `aborted`, else `other`.
- Cache miss: `cacheRead === 0` and input + cacheRead + cacheWrite >= `CACHE_MISS_MIN_INPUT`.
- The context histogram counts only turns with input > 0. Tier tokens: a turn with input > `CONTEXT_TIER_EDGE` (strictly above).
- Prompts before any user message are counted in buckets and tools but not in prompt stats.
- Unknown entry types and non-JSON lines are counted in `skipped` and never throw. Known types that are not read (for example `codemode-store`) are not counted.
- Surface, `pigna` and project are placeholders in `emptyFacts` (`terminal`, false, `projectOf(cwd)`). See Risks.
- `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` stays 1: nothing is cached yet.
- Design doc `## Usage` > Per-file facts updated for the rules above (resume, skip rules, error categories, wall time).

## Files Touched
- `src/main/usage-extract.ts` (new): `extractFileUsage({ root, path }, previous?)`.
- `src/main/usage-extract.test.ts` (new): 12 tests.
- `src/shared/usage.ts`: `FileUsageFacts` gains `consumedBytes`, `skipped` and `resume`. New types `PendingCall`, `OpenPrompt`, `UsageResume`.
- `docs/DESIGN.md`: `## Usage` > Per-file facts.

## Interfaces Changed
- `extractFileUsage(target: { root: SourceRoot; path: string }, previous?: FileUsageFacts): Promise<FileUsageFacts | undefined>`. Returns undefined when the file has no session header. Throws only when `stat` or the read fails. T05 must catch per-file errors.
- `FileUsageFacts` new fields: `consumedBytes: number`, `skipped: { lines: number; entries: number }`, `resume: UsageResume`. `size` and `mtimeMs` are the stat taken before the read.
- `session.lastAt` is the last entry's timestamp in file order; it is the resume clock.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm test`: 158 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,466 tests passed, 3 skipped. `src/main/usage-extract.test.ts`: 12/12.
- Tests cover: tool round trip; parallel calls, one error, and a codemode call with nested calls; error and aborted turns with prompt abort and step histogram; compaction and context edit; abandoned branch (its turns counted); hour buckets, tier tokens, cache miss and context histogram; active time with the 5 min cap; subagent status and session name; bad lines, unknown types and role text inside a string; no header returns undefined; torn last line; incremental append from mid-line equals a full read (with a pending tool call across the cut).
- Real-file checks (scratch bench outside the repo, not committed): largest file totals match Python (see Facts Learned).

Performance on this Mac (scratch bench, esbuild bundle, one Node process per run, `/usr/bin/time -l`):

| run | files | data | time | max RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| extract, largest file | 1 | 115.5 MB | 0.16 s (runs: 164, 160, 158 ms) | 151 MB |
| parse-every-line baseline, largest file | 1 | 115.5 MB | 0.34 s | 185 MB |
| extract, whole history | 1,675 | 2,828 MB | 5.9 s, one thread | 447 MB |
| parse-every-line baseline, whole history | 1,675 | 2,828 MB | 8.4 s | 344 MB |
| no-op incremental read, largest file | 1 | 0 bytes | 0 ms, buckets identical | - |

The prefilter gains about 1.4x overall. Tool results (76% of bytes) must still be parsed for their ids, timestamps and error flags. Whole-history cold index is 5.9 s single-thread, well under the 30 s budget.

Lint: the repo has no lint script; typecheck covers the touched files.
No external docs were used; Node `fs` streams and `Buffer` only.

## Risks
- **Surface classification seam (plan defect for T04).** The extractor sees the system message and the first user message in passing but does not keep them. T04 needs them for markers and the ATP prefix. Options: an extractor hook that receives those signals, or a head-only classifier that reads the first lines. T04 should decide this before T05 relies on surfaces.
- **Resume trusts append-only files.** A file rewritten to a larger size with a different prefix would resume from `consumedBytes` and merge wrongly. The index's size and mtime check triggers a read, but `extractFileUsage` cannot detect the rewrite. T05 should do a full read when the file's head changes, or accept the risk for pi's own writes.
- **Tool durations** are upper bounds for parallel calls (as in T01).
- **Memory**: the whole-history run peaks at 447 MB RSS. The largest-file run peaks at 151 MB. The workers in T05 should be sized with that in mind.
- `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` stays 1 because nothing is cached; any cache written before the surface seam is fixed must be discarded.

## Recommended Next Step
T03 (price snapshot) can run in parallel. Before T05, T04 should settle how the surface signals reach classification (see Risks), and set `session.surface`, `pigna` and `project` on the facts. T05 calls `extractFileUsage(target, previous)` per file in its worker pool. If the 30 s budget ever gets tight, the next lever is skipping toolResult `content` without parsing it (about 76% of the bytes); that is not needed for now.

T03_pricing_table.title: Resolve model prices from pi's installed model data
T03_pricing_table.instruction:
Goal: src/main/usage-pricing.ts gives a price per provider+model so claude-bridge turns (recorded cost 0) get an API-equivalent estimate. No network and no dependency on the pi package.

Steps:
1. Locate the pi install the way PiAuth does (src/main/pi-auth.ts resolves the @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent package that `pi` or PIGNA_PI_BIN points to), then read node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/data/*.json. Each model has cost {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite} in USD per 1M tokens and optional tiers [{inputTokensAbove, ...}]. Also read custom model costs from ~/.pi/agent/models.json ($PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR).
2. Lookup order: exact provider+model; then a provider alias (claude-bridge -> anthropic; document others found in real data); then the model id under any provider. Otherwise the model is unpriced.
3. A pure costOf(usage, price) in src/shared that applies tiers per turn (the context of the turn decides the tier).
4. Cache the table in memory; reload when the pi install changes.

Tests: tier selection, the alias, an unpriced model, a models.json override, a missing pi install (empty table, no throw).
Acceptance: tests pass; the node report lists which real models (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-sol, ...) are priced and from where.

T03_pricing_table.report:
## Outcome
DONE. Model prices now come from pi's installed pi-ai data plus the user's `models.json`, read at runtime and cached until either changes. `costOf(usage, price)` is pure and applies tiers per turn. Commit `96a7d64`.

**Plan defect, blocks T02 and T05:** the design says the price table has one tier edge (272,000). The real table has three: 100,000, 200,000 and 272,000. The facts store only tokens above 272,000, so turns between 100k and 272k are priced wrong. See Risks.

## Facts Learned
- pi-ai data: `<pi-coding-agent>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/data/*.json` (42 files, pi-ai 1.0.4, `.manifest.json` has `generatedAt`). Grouped by API, then `chat:<id>`. Each entry has `provider`, `id`, `cost` and optional `cost.tiers`. The bundle chunks hold the same data; not used.
- pi-ai `calculateCost` (`pi-ai/dist/models.js:657`): the tier is the highest whose `inputTokensAbove` is below `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`. The whole turn is priced at its rates. `cacheWrite1h` is charged at 2x input.
- Tier edges in the real data: 272000 (65 entries), 200000 (xAI grok-4.3/4.5/4.6/4.7, GitHub Copilot grok-4.5/4.6/4.7 and gpt-5.6-luna, radius grok-4.7), and 100000 (the user's `models.json` haiku).
- pi's `models.json` merge (`pi-coding-agent/dist/core/provider-composer.js`): a `models` entry with the same id replaces the model, and a missing `cost` defaults to zero. `modelOverrides[id].cost` merges per field; `tiers` replaces when given.
- No session file has a `cacheWrite1h` usage field (checked all of `~/.pi/agent/sessions`). The 5-minute rate assumption holds for existing data.
- Real models and where their prices come from (`loadPriceTable` on this Mac):

- **Tier edges (plan defect).** The facts keep tokens only above 272,000 (`CONTEXT_TIER_EDGE`). T04_classify_sessions.title: Classify sessions by surface and fold worktrees into projects
T04_classify_sessions.instruction:
Goal: a pure module src/shared/usage-classify.ts that maps a session (header cwd, file location, the markers T01 chose) to {project, surface, isPigna}.

Steps:
1. Fold ~/.pi-gna/worktrees/<id>/<original absolute path> into the original project and keep the card id (src/main/worktree.ts has the layout).
2. Surfaces as decided in T01: pi-gna chat, card worktree, ATP worker or orchestrator (atp-sessions root, src/main/atp-threads.ts), subagent, CI runner (cwd under actions-runner style folders: group them under one 'CI runners' project per repo), terminal pi.
3. A pi-gna marker test that works on historical files, e.g. pi-gna's bridge tools in the system message's toolsAdded or sections.
4. Project display names: the last path segments, unique among projects.

Tests with real-looking paths taken from ~/.pi/agent/sessions folder names (no private content).

T04_classify_sessions.context: Project: a Usage dashboard in pi-gna's Settings (new section 'Usage', group pi-gna) with in-depth, local-only analytics of how pi and pi-gna were used: tokens by type, estimated cost, models, projects, pi-gna surfaces (chats, card worktrees, ATP workers, subagents), tools, activity over time, agent health and behaviour insights. Nothing leaves the machine: no network for pricing or anything else.
T04_classify_sessions.report:
## Outcome
DONE. The pure classifier `src/shared/usage-classify.ts` maps a session to `{ project, surface, isPigna, card }`, the extractor (`src/main/usage-extract.ts`) now records the pi-gna markers and classifies every file in `finish()`, and the node's tests pass. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass, except one unrelated timing flake (see Verification). Commit `0d71cb2`.

## Facts Learned
- Session header `parentSession` is the parent's session id (not a path). A subagent file sits in `<parent dir>/tasks/`, and the parent file is that directory's parent path plus `.jsonl`. All 435 subagents in `~/.pi/agent/sessions` resolve that way.
- The ATP store (`~/Library/Application Support/pi-gna/atp-sessions`) holds three kinds of top-level chat, all with `cwd` under the project or its card worktree: 223 workers (first prompt is the runtime packet, system `addendum` says `You are an ATP worker in pi-gna`), 19 orchestrators (system `addendum` says `You are the orchestrator of an ATP plan in pi-gna`, first prompt is the user's), and subagents in `tasks/` whose system `preamble` carries the worker text.
- Pi-gna markers by section, across 1,098 top-level and subagent files with a system message: `kanban_`, `lament`, `threads_` appear only in the system `rules` section; `pigna-visual-prompt` in `project_context` (and occasionally `preamble`). No marker hit comes from user project instructions alone.
- Some `sessions` files carry the ATP runtime packet as their first prompt (2 files), so the packet test is needed beyond the `atp` root.
- 330 older top-level sessions (mostly June to September, plus `piolium` audit runs) have no system message at all. Nothing in them can say pi-gna or not.
- Live check on the last 30 days: 1,377 files in window (930 top-level sessions, 447 subagents). The system-message detection (`"message":{"role":"system"` in the first 512 bytes) matches the earlier Python survey to within one file written during the run (1,348 of 1,678 files).

## Decisions Made
- Surface order (first match): subagent (path in `tasks/` and a `parentId`), then `atp-worker` (root `atp` or the runtime packet), then `ci` (`actions-runner(s)/` in cwd), then `card` (cwd in `~/.pi-gna/worktrees/<id>/`), then `pigna-chat` (system names a pi-gna marker), else `terminal`. `isPigna` is true for atp-worker, card and pigna-chat, and for a subagent whose parent is pigna. CI is not pi-gna.
- The ATP orchestrator is counted as `atp-worker`. It is not a surface in v1 (DESIGN out-of-scope list), so `SURFACES` is unchanged. The marker to split it later is the system addendum text above.
- Project key: `projectOf(cwd)` (card worktrees fold into their project); CI sessions get `ci:<repo>` (segment after `/_work/`), so every runner of one repository is one project.
- The card id is kept on every session that ran in a card worktree (`SessionMeta.card`), including subagents of such a chat.
- Labels (`projectLabels`): the last folder names, extended per project only until labels are unique. CI labels read `CI runners (<repo>)`.
- Markers are stored in the facts (`markers: { systemMessage, pignaTools, atpRuntime }`), so classification never needs a re-read. `atpRuntime` is taken from the first prompt only.
- "Unclassified" = a `terminal` session whose file has no system message. Terminal is the fallback for pi-gna chats with every feature off, so those are not proven terminal; the no-system ones have no evidence either way.
- Facts version bumped 1 to 2 (new `markers` field and `SessionMeta.card`). No cache exists yet, so nothing is invalidated in practice.
- Placed the module in `src/shared/` as this node says (DESIGN had `src/main/`), since it is pure and T06 and the renderer may import it; DESIGN's file list is updated to match.
- Subagent `pigna` is provisional in the extractor (false) because the parent is not known from one file. The index (T05) must set it from the parent's facts (see Risks / Recommended Next Step).

## Files Touched
- `src/shared/usage-classify.ts` (new): `PIGNA_MARKERS`, `ATP_RUNTIME_PREFIX`, `SessionEvidence`, `SessionPlacement`, `projectKey`, `classifySession`, `namesPignaTools`, `startsAtpRuntime`, `projectLabels`.

- `src/main/usage-extract.test.ts`: 3 tests on markers and classification (card chat, ATP claim packet first prompt only, no system message).
- `src/shared/usage.ts`: `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` 2; `SessionMeta.card?`; `SessionMarkers`; `FileUsageFacts.markers`.
- `src/shared/usage.test.ts`: version assertion now 2.

- `docs/DESIGN.md`: file list (classify now in `src/shared`), surface rules with the measured counts, the markers in Per-file facts, project labels, and the ATP orchestrator and subagent-pigna open items.

## Interfaces Changed
- `src/shared/usage-classify.ts`:
  - `classifySession(evidence: SessionEvidence, parentPigna = false): SessionPlacement`. `SessionEvidence` = `{ root, path, cwd, parentId?, markers }`; `SessionPlacement` = `{ project, surface, isPigna, card? }`.
  - `projectKey(cwd): string`, `projectLabels(projects): Map<string, string>`, `namesPignaTools(text: { includes(search: string): boolean }): boolean` (works on a string or a Buffer), `startsAtpRuntime(prompt: string): boolean`.
  - Constants: `PIGNA_MARKERS`, `ATP_RUNTIME_PREFIX`.
- `src/shared/board.ts`: new export `cardOfWorktree(cwd): string | undefined`.
- `src/shared/usage.ts`: `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION = 2`; `SessionMeta.card?: string`; new `SessionMarkers`; `FileUsageFacts.markers: SessionMarkers`.
- `extractFileUsage` now returns `session.surface`, `session.pigna`, `session.project`, `session.card` classified (subagent `pigna` provisional, see Risks).

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0 (after the change; first attempt failed on `Buffer` in a shared test, fixed by removing that case: `src/shared` is not typed with Node types).
- `pnpm vitest run src/shared/usage-classify.test.ts src/main/usage-extract.test.ts src/shared/usage.test.ts`: 3 files, 30 tests, all pass.
- `pnpm test`: 160 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,496 tests passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed: `src/main/updater.test.ts > SWAP_SCRIPT > waits for pi-gna to exit, swaps in the staged app and starts it` (ENOENT on the `launched` file after 1.7 s under parallel load). Run alone, `updater.test.ts` passes 14/14 twice; the failing test is not touched by this change.
- Lint: the repo has no lint script or lint config (no eslint, biome or prettier file), so typecheck is the check that fits.
- Real-file survey (one-off vitest file, deleted before commit; results in `/tmp/t04-survey.json`): the real `extractFileUsage` and `classifySession` over all 1,678 session files (1,428 in `sessions`, 246 in `atp`, subagents included) in 6.8 s. Last 30 days (1,377 files in window):

| surface | top-level sessions | subagents | isPigna |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pigna-chat | 302 | 0 | 302 |
| card | 133 | 0 | 133 |
| atp-worker | 237 (15 orchestrators) | 0 | 237 |
| ci | 54 | 0 | 0 |
| terminal | 204 (29 with no system message) | 0 | 0 |
| subagent | 0 | 447 | 99 (their parent is pigna) |

  Unclassified: 29 terminal sessions with no system message (28 under `casus-review`, 1 under `torntools_extension`). Distinct card ids in window: 127. Distinct project keys: 15.
- Not run: no app or UI check (no UI in this node).

## Risks
- Subagent `pigna` is false until the index passes the parent's flag. Any consumer that reads `session.pigna` before T05 is wired sees subagents as non-pi-gna. The survey above used the parent's flag.
- The orchestrator shares the `atp-worker` surface, so "ATP workers" in the Surfaces panel includes orchestrators (15 of 237 in the last 30 days). A split needs a surface name in `SURFACES`, which DESIGN defers.
- The 29 no-system-message sessions and any pi-gna chat with every pi-gna feature off are counted as terminal; the no-system ones are shown as unclassified only in this report, not yet in the Usage page.
- `lament` as a marker is a plain substring. It matched only the `rules` section in the real files, but any user project prompt that says `lament` in its system message (for example a rule about this word) would mark a terminal chat as pi-gna.
- The marker scan of each system message runs on the whole line (only when its first 512 bytes hold the system role); cost is inside the cold-index budget, not measured on the full history.

T05 (index): after `extractFileUsage` for every file, set each subagent's `session.pigna` from its parent's facts: the parent path is the subagent path up to `/tasks/` plus `.jsonl`, and the call is `classifySession({ root, path, cwd, parentId, markers }, parentFacts.session.pigna)`. T05_usage_index.title: Build the cached, incremental usage index off the main thread
T05_usage_index.instruction:
Goal: src/main/usage-index.ts keeps FileUsageFacts for every session file under the roots T01 chose, cached on disk, without blocking the main process.

Steps:
1. Walk the roots (sessionsDir() and userData/atp-sessions). For each file compare path+size+mtime with the cache: unchanged means reuse; grown means an incremental extract from the stored offset (T02); changed otherwise means a full re-extract; removed files are dropped. Attach the classification (T04).
2. Run extraction in a worker_thread (check how electron-vite bundles extra entries; src/main/index.ts and electron.vite.config.ts) with bounded concurrency. Emit progress {done, total, bytes}.
3. Persist to userData/usage-index.json with a version number and atomic temp-file rename, like persistSessionIndex in src/main/session-index.ts. A version mismatch or damaged file means a rebuild.
4. Expose: ensureIndexed(onProgress), refreshFile(path) (later called after a run settles), allFacts().
5. Apply the dedupe rule from T01 across files.

Tests: a temp sessions dir with fixtures covering new, grown, rewritten and deleted files, a cache round trip and a version bump.
Acceptance: tests pass; against the real data (read-only) the node report gives cold and warm index times, peak RSS and cache file size, compared with the T01 budget. The main thread must never block for more than about 50 ms at a time.

T05_usage_index.report:
## Outcome
DONE. `src/main/usage-index.ts` (class `UsageIndex`) keeps `FileUsageFacts` for every `*.jsonl` under the `sessions` and `atp` roots, cached in a file, with incremental updates. Extraction runs in worker_threads (`src/main/usage-worker.ts`, a second electron-vite main entry). Real-data bench (read-only sources, cache written to /tmp): cold 6.4 s, warm 0.19 s, 1,682 files, cache 3.8 MB, main-thread event-loop max 33 ms cold and 39 ms warm. Commit `b45d3d2`.

## Facts Learned
- electron-vite emits a second main entry with `main.build.rollupOptions.input` (`index` and `usage-worker`). `out/main/usage-worker.js` is ESM, imports a shared chunk `./chunks/board-*.js`, and has no electron or log import.
- Head check: fixtures under 4 KB make a whole-file hash change on every append, so the head must be compared over the length recorded at extraction (`headBytes`), not a fixed 4 KB.
- Real data: 1,682 files (2.84 GB) and 1,682 facts, so no session id collisions in the data. Surfaces over the whole history: terminal 505, subagent 447, pigna-chat 304, atp-worker 239, card 133, ci 54.
- Bench, 4 workers (`min(4, cores-1)` on 8 cores): cold 6.4 s, warm 0.19 s, second warm 0.06 s. Peak RSS 626 MB in the bench process (vitest included); 633 MB and 644 MB on the warm runs.
- Main-thread event-loop delay (monitorEventLoopDelay, forks pool so the test runs on a real main thread): cold max 32.9 ms, p99 6 ms; warm max 38.6 ms, p99 38.6 ms (the block is the cache's JSON.parse).

## Decisions Made
- Extraction is injected as `openExtractor: () => Extractor`, opened per run and closed when it settles. Production uses `openWorkerExtractor(workerFile, size)`, a pool of `size` workers with one request per worker; a dead worker fails its request and is respawned. Vitest cannot run a TS worker file, so tests pass in-process `extractFileUsage`; the real worker is exercised by the bench against the built bundle.
- Cache entry: `[path, { head, headBytes, facts }]`. A file is resumed only when it grew AND `headOf(path, headBytes) === head`. Same size with a new mtime, or a shrink, is read in full.
- Files with no session header are not cached and are re-read on every run.
- Runs and `refreshFile` are serialized through one queue; the cache is loaded once. `ensureIndexed` reports `{ done, total, bytes }` after every file (unchanged files included). Throttling to 250 ms is T08's (`usage.progress`).
- Save: temp file plus rename. A damaged JSON or a version mismatch or a malformed entry rebuilds the whole cache (warned in the log).
- Dedupe: `allFacts()` keeps one facts per session id, the one with the larger `consumedBytes` (then newer mtime). Applies across roots too. No effect on the real data.
- Subagent `pigna`: after every run and every `refreshFile`, `classifySubagents` re-runs `classifySession` for each subagent with its parent's flag (parent = path before `/tasks/` + `.jsonl`). A subagent whose parent is not indexed stays false.
- Not wired into `src/main/index.ts` and no IPC: T08 wires `ensureIndexed` and the host API.

## Files Touched
- `electron.vite.config.ts`: `main.build.rollupOptions.input` adds `usage-worker`.
- `src/main/usage-worker.ts` (new): one request at a time, replies `{ id, facts }` or `{ id, error }`.
- `src/main/usage-index.ts` (new): `UsageIndex`, `openWorkerExtractor`, `defaultConcurrency`, types `Extractor`, `Extract`, `IndexProgress`, `UsageIndexOptions`.
- `src/main/usage-index.test.ts` (new): 12 tests.
- `docs/DESIGN.md`: `## Usage` cache paragraph (entry shape, head rule, measured size), Open items (subagent pigna settled), Performance budget (measured numbers).

## Interfaces Changed
- `new UsageIndex({ roots: Record<SourceRoot, string>, file: string, openExtractor: () => Extractor, concurrency: number })`.
- `ensureIndexed(onProgress?: (p: IndexProgress) => void): Promise<void>`; `refreshFile(path: string): Promise<void>`; `allFacts(): FileUsageFacts[]`.
- `openWorkerExtractor(workerFile: string, size: number): Extractor`; `defaultConcurrency(): number`.
- `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` unchanged (2); the cache file's own `version` is the same constant.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/main/usage-index.test.ts`: 12/12 (first run, unchanged, grown resumes and equals a full read, rewrite with same size, grown with changed head, deleted, cache reuse across instances, version bump and damaged cache, dedupe, subagent parent flag, failing file isolated, refreshFile).

## Outcome
DONE. `buildCoreReport` in `src/shared/usage-report.ts` is a pure function over the facts, the price table, the query and `now`. It returns the core parts of the report: headline, daily series, weekday x hour grid, models, projects and top sessions. Commit `a5de3d1`. Typecheck and the full test suite pass. The 2,000-file build measures 8–15 ms warm (30d and all-time), about 30 ms on the first cold call. That is under the 100 ms target.

## Facts Learned
- Real-file check, one-off: 166 `claude-haiku-5-5` turns in the sessions, 9 of them with context in (100k, 272k]. The input and output understatement from the missing 100k edge is $0.03 (cacheRead and cacheWrite not counted).
- Thinking level is recorded per file (`FileUsageFacts.thinking`), not per model, so a per-model thinking split cannot be built from the facts.
- Prompts, tool calls and active time are whole-file totals (no time bucketing below the hour). Range filtering is exact only for turns, tokens, cost and sessions.

## Decisions Made
- Signature: `buildCoreReport(facts, query, prices, now, files)`. It returns `CoreUsageReport` (the `UsageReport` minus surfaces, tools, health, windows, insights), so T07 adds those parts and T08 composes them. `files` is passed in because the pure function cannot count unindexed files. `timeZone` comes from `query.timeZone`, defaulting to the Mac's zone.
- Range: a file counts when one of its hour buckets falls in the range. A bucket is placed by its midpoint (hour + 30 min), so buckets are hour-precise and whole-hour offsets are exact. Presets end at the next hour boundary after `now`, so the current hour is included. Local midnight is found from the zone's offset (two passes, DST-safe).
- Local day, weekday and hour are memoised per distinct hour bucket (one `Intl` call each).
- Estimated cost per bucket: the part above the tier edge (`tierTokens`) at the highest tier at or below 272k (`largeContextRates`), the rest at base rates. This is per bucket, not per turn. `costOf` is unchanged in behaviour; the formula moved to `priceTokens`.
- Unpriced buckets add nothing to `estimated`. They are counted in `unpricedTurns` and `unpricedShare`.
- Streaks run over the range's days. The current streak ends on the last day, or the day before while the last day has no turns.
- Sessions: top 10 by estimated cost (ties: tokens, then id). A subagent rolls into its parent when the parent is in scope. `openable` is `pigna` and no parent.
- Projects are ordered by estimate, then tokens, then project key. Labels come from `projectLabels`. `sessions` counts files, subagents included.
- Models are ordered by estimate, then tokens, then `provider/model`. `topModel` is the first row.

## Files Touched
- `src/shared/usage-report.ts` (new): `buildCoreReport`, `CoreUsageReport`, the zone clock, range and streak helpers.
- `src/shared/usage-report.test.ts` (new): 16 tests. Fixed zone (New York) with spring-forward and fall-back days; the local 7d range; source and project filters; range by turns; cost split (estimated vs recorded, unpriced shown); tier pricing per bucket; cache hit rate; streaks (longest, current, the grace day); models order and shares; subagent rollup and session order; worktree folding and labels; empty all-time and empty fixed ranges.

## Interfaces Changed
- `src/shared/usage.ts`, additive:
  - `CostTotals.unpricedShare: number` (billed-token share on unpriced turns).
  - `UsageTotals.currentStreak`, `longestStreak: number`; `topModel: string | null`.
  - `ModelRow.share`, `cacheHitRate: number`.
  - `ProjectRow.lastAt: number`.
- `src/shared/usage-prices.ts`: `priceTokens(tokens, rates): number`; `largeContextRates(price): ModelRates`.
- `src/shared/usage-report.ts`: `CoreUsageReport = Omit<UsageReport, "surfaces" | "tools" | "health" | "windows" | "insights">`; `buildCoreReport(facts, query, prices, now, files): CoreUsageReport`.
- Not built: the thinking-level split per model (see Risks).

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm test`: 164 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,538 tests passed, 3 skipped. The 16 new report tests and the 9 price tests pass.
- Performance (temporary vitest file, deleted): 2,000 synthetic session files, 1 to 20 buckets each (about 20k buckets), 40 projects, five provider/model keys, Europe/Rome. Build time in ms over 7 runs. 30d: 29.7 (cold), then 13.9, 11.6, 9.8, 10.1, 9.0, 8.3. All-time: 18.4 (cold), then 13.7–14.8. 7d: 2.3–2.6.
- No lint script or lint config exists in the repo; typecheck and tests are the checks.
- No UI touched.

## Risks
- **Tier edges (open from T03, still open).** The facts keep tokens above 272k only, so turns in (100k, 272k] for haiku, and (200k, 272k] for the 200k-tier models, are priced at base rates. Measured on this Mac: $0.03 understated on input and output. The fix (per-edge tokens in `UsageBucket`, `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` bump) touches T01 and T02 and needs the orchestrator's decision.
- **Per-model thinking split** is not in the facts. The models table has no thinking split; the node asked for one. Needs a fact change (per-model thinking counts) in T02.
- **File-level totals under time ranges.** A file with a turn in range counts all its prompts, tool calls and active time, even the part before the range start. This over-counts for a long chat that straddles the start of a 7d range.

## Outcome

Commit `b4e9844` holds the coherent partial work so a follow-up can build on it.

## Facts Learned
- `ToolStat` has no per-call durations, so median and p90 are impossible from the facts. Mean duration works.
- Prompts, tools, stops, errors, compactions and context histograms are whole-file totals. They cannot be bucketed in time, so "stop reasons over time" is delivered as range totals.
- Rate-limit hits per window are not derivable: error categories are per file, not per hour.

Burn rate is tokens per minute over elapsed time, capped at the block end or now. The top 5 by tokens are returned, plus `current` (the active block).
- Rate-limit hits per window are dropped from `WindowRow`; DESIGN now says so.
- Insights: rules fire at share >= 10% (`INSIGHT_MIN_SHARE`). Each carries share, count, base, value, threshold and a one-line tip. At most 6 are kept, sorted by share then id. `compactions` uses prompts per compaction against a threshold of 10. New rules: `bash-errors` and `expensive-subagents` (subagent estimate on models with list output >= `EXPENSIVE_OUTPUT_RATE`, 15 USD per M).

## Outcome
DONE. `usage.get({ query? })` (remote, read-only) and `usage.refresh` (remote, mutating) are in the host API, the host core, the IPC routes and the desktop preload (`window.studio.usage`). `usage.progress` is a global event, forwarded to the desktop as `usageProgress`. The main-side `UsageService` owns one index and the price table per launch. Commit `9bc282f`. `pnpm typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm test` 166 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,576 tests passed, 3 skipped. A dev-run over the real session files returns a report (numbers below). The Electron app itself was not launched.

## Facts Learned
- `sessionsDir()` reads `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` at call time, and the login shell can set it after launch. The index roots therefore have to be read at scan time, and the first scan has to wait for `piDirs`.
- `buildCoreReport` already sets `meta.indexedFiles` from the source filter (`sourced.length`), so the service only supplies `files`.
- Real data (this Mac, 1,685 files, 4 worker threads): cold `usage.get` 2.5 s; warm 30-day pigna 76 ms; all-time 64 ms. The warm report equals the cold one. Response sizes: 28.6 KB (30d, pigna), 52 KB (all, all sources).
- 30-day pigna totals: 33,827 turns, 778 sessions indexed, est. $1,903.61, cache hit 97.9%, 157 error turns. The surfaces match the T04 numbers (pigna-chat 304, card 133, atp-worker 242 over the whole history).
- Before the caps, the models and projects lists were uncapped (31 projects and 19 models over all-time on this Mac). The tool list was uncapped too (about 60 tool names in this data, so the cap of 50 is close).
- `buildBehaviourReport` computes insights from the full tool list, so the tool cap applies only to the output; `topFailing` is unchanged.

## Decisions Made
- `usage.get` args are `{ query?: UsageQuery }`. An omitted query means `{ range: "30d", source: "pigna" }` (the DESIGN default). The query is checked by `parseUsageQuery` (`src/main/usage-service.ts`) and bad input is `bad_request` before the report runs. Checks: presets or `{ from, to }` with `from < to` and at most 4,000 days apart (this bounds the daily series); `source` is pigna or all; `project` is at most 1,024 characters; `timeZone` is a valid IANA zone.
- `usage.refresh` is remote and mutating, because it rewrites `usage-index.json`. A phone needs an `Idempotency-Key` for it. It is not in `READ_ONLY_METHODS`.
- `usage.get` is in `READ_ONLY_METHODS` and remote. Aggregates only (see the threat model rows).
- Lifecycle: `UsageService.get` awaits one scan per launch (`ready`). The scan waits for `piDirs`, reads the roots at scan time and stores the facts in memory. `refresh` runs another scan. Overlapping scans are coalesced. A failed first scan is retried by the next `get`.
- Progress: published on the global hub (phones get it through the SSE stream), and forwarded to the desktop as `IPC.usageProgress` ("usage:progress"). Throttled to 250 ms, with `scan` and `done` always sent. The last event is `done` with `total = discovered`.
- Bounds (applied in the pure report, so the totals still count every row): models 30, projects 50, tools 50. Sessions 10, windows 5 and insights 6 were already bounded.
- `meta.files` = session files found on disk in both roots. `meta.indexedFiles` = those the source covers. For `pigna`, `indexedFiles` is below `files` even when everything is indexed. This is documented in DESIGN.
- The mobile client needs no code change. `HostClient.call` is typed from `HostMethods`, so `c.call("usage.get", { query })` is typed. Phone UI is T16.

- `src/shared/host-api.ts`: `usage.get`, `usage.refresh` in `HostMethods`; `usage.progress` in `GlobalEvent`; `usage.get` in `READ_ONLY_METHODS`.

- `src/preload/index.ts`: `usage.get`, `usage.refresh`, `usage.onProgress`.

- `src/main/usage-service.test.ts` (new): 11 tests, using a temp sessions dir and the in-process extractor.

## Facts Learned
- Naive reader (full `JSON.parse` of every line, no shared code): 1,686 files (1,431 sessions, 255 ATP), 0 unparseable lines, 0 torn tails, parsed in 10 to 12 s.
- Last run, 14 days: 46,979 assistant turns; billed 7.87 billion tokens (input 16.2 M, output 44.0 M, cacheRead 7.64 billion, cacheWrite 172.4 M; reasoning 18.5 M inside output); cache hit 97.6%; 265 error turns; estimated 2,824 USD at list price; recorded 164 USD.

- History: 100,017 turns, 1,686 files, 7,363 USD estimated.

- claude-opus-5-5: 35,815 turns in range, 2,541.53 USD on both sides with 4 / 20 / 0.20 / 5 rates. Hand-computed turn (6 Oct 2026): 0.220915 USD.

- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm test`: 166 files passed, 2 skipped (the real-data test is skipped without its env var); 1,576 tests passed, 4 skipped.

T10_chart_primitives.report:
## Outcome
DONE. Six themed SVG/CSS chart components are in `src/renderer/src/components/Charts.tsx`: StackedBars (ResizeObserver width, crosshair, rich tooltip), CalendarHeatmap (GitHub-style), MatrixHeatmap (weekday x hour), HBars (ranked, value and share), SplitBar (100% stacked), Sparkline. Plus Legend and HeatScale. Pure helpers (nice ticks, stable colour assignment, heat levels, calendar frames) are in `chart-scale.ts` with tests. Light, dark and a project palette were checked in a throwaway story (not committed). Commit `24502b9`.

## Facts Learned
- The app's theme sets `--accent`, `--secondary`, `--highlight`, `--ok`, `--warn`, `--bad` on `<html>` (lib/theme.ts). A `:root` rule that uses `var(--accent)` therefore follows project palettes, because it resolves on the same element.
- Dark is the default `:root`; light is `:root[data-theme-mode="light"]` or the system light media query on `:root:not([data-theme-mode])`.
- `formatTokens` (lib/format.ts) cannot show billions or fractions for axis ticks, so `formatCompact` was added beside it.
- The renderer had no chart code, no tooltip component and no focus-aware pattern; TurnRail's `role="tooltip"` is the only precedent.
- In the pi-gna browser pane the page does not have window focus (`document.hasFocus()` is false). `element.focus()` sets `activeElement` but may not fire focus events. Real key presses (browser_press) do reach the chart. Pointer hover was driven with dispatched `pointerover`/`pointermove` events.
- Hash-based colour slots alone gave two models the same colour (Opus and Haiku, both `--chart-3`) in the fixture. Per-chart probing fixed it.
- Sources: no external docs were consulted. ResizeObserver, `color-mix()`, `vectorEffect`, and Tailwind v4 utilities are already used in this repo or are long-stable web platform features. No web search was needed for this node.

## Decisions Made
- Colours come only from CSS: `--chart-1` to `--chart-8` in styles.css, derived from the theme's accent, ok, warn, secondary, highlight, muted and bad via `color-mix`. Chart components reference only these variables and `--line`, `--fg`, `--muted`, `--faint`, `--raised`, `--canvas`, `--font-mono`.
- `colorScale(keys)`: each key takes its FNV-1a hash slot. Keys are processed in sorted order and a collision probes to the next free slot. A key keeps its colour while its chart keeps its neighbours, and the keys of one chart never share a colour (up to 8). This is stable per model, not guaranteed across different key sets.
- `bad` (red) is the last slot, so a project's largest category is not red by default.
- Interactive charts (StackedBars, both heat grids, SplitBar) are focusable (`tabIndex=0`, `role="img"`, `aria-label` = required `summary` prop, `aria-describedby` = tooltip id while shown). Arrow keys move the cursor; the same tooltip shows for pointer and keyboard. HBars and Sparkline are non-interactive and have no tooltip.
- Heat levels use the square root of value / max, with 4 levels plus empty. Empty cells are `color-mix(fg 7%)`; levels mix `--accent` at 25 / 45 / 68 / 92%.
- Heatmap geometry is measured from the container width; cells are clamped (calendar 5 to 13 px, matrix 8 to 18 px wide, 14 px tall). The calendar is Monday-first, with weekday labels Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun. A day outside the data's first and last date is blank.
- Tooltip flips to the left of the anchor past half the width.
- Phone: not done. DESIGN.md puts full phone charts out of scope for v1 (T16 shows a compact summary); `src/mobile` is untouched.
- DESIGN.md `## Usage` > Metrics and layout gained a short paragraph on the chart kit (the only doc change).

## Files Touched
- `src/renderer/src/components/Charts.tsx` (new): StackedBars, CalendarHeatmap, MatrixHeatmap, HBars, SplitBar, Sparkline, Legend, HeatScale; types Series, Bucket, Amount.
- `src/renderer/src/components/chart-scale.ts` (new): niceTicks, colorSlot, chartColor, colorScale, heatLevel, heatFill, everyNth, formatShare, addDays, dayOffset, weekdayIndex, calendarFrame, formatDay, monthName, WEEKDAYS.
- `src/renderer/src/components/chart-scale.test.ts` (new): ticks, colour slots and scale, heat levels, calendar frames, labels and shares.
- `src/renderer/src/lib/format.ts`: `formatCompact` (B, M, k; two significant digits below 10).
- `src/renderer/src/lib/lib.test.ts`: `formatCompact` assertions beside the `formatTokens` ones.
- `src/renderer/src/styles.css`: `:root` block with `--chart-1` to `--chart-8`.
- `docs/DESIGN.md`: one paragraph under `## Usage` > Metrics and layout.

## Interfaces Changed
- `Charts.tsx` exports:
  - `StackedBars({ series: Series[], buckets: {label, values: Record<key, number>}[], format, summary, height? })`
  - `CalendarHeatmap({ days: {date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', value}[], format, summary })`
  - `MatrixHeatmap({ rows: string[], cols: string[], values: number[][] (values[row][col]), format, summary })`
  - `HBars({ rows: {key, label, value}[], format, summary })`
  - `SplitBar({ parts: {key, label, value}[], format, summary })`
  - `Sparkline({ values, summary, color? })`
  - `Legend({ items: {key, label}[] })`
  - `HeatScale({ low?, high? })`
- `format` is any `(n: number) => string`. Pass `formatTokens`, `formatCompact` or `formatCost`. The axis always uses `formatCompact`.
- `summary` is required on every chart and is the aria-label. The caller writes it.
- `chart-scale.ts` and `formatCompact` as listed above.
- Tokens: `--chart-1` to `--chart-8` are new CSS custom properties on `:root`.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0 (after the final change).
- `pnpm test`: 162 files passed, 1 skipped; 1,509 tests passed, 3 skipped (the T01 report recorded 157 files / 1,454 tests; the difference includes the T02 to T04 tests and this node's tests).
- No lint script exists in package.json, and the repo has no prettier config, so no formatter was run.
- Throwaway story (Vite on 127.0.0.1:5199, fixture data, deleted before commit; the server was stopped):
  - Dark: all charts render, including the 320 px column (ResizeObserver) and the empty state.
  - Light, with `palette=warm` (accent terracotta, secondary green, and so on): colours follow the palette.
  - Keyboard: focus the stacked bars and press ArrowLeft; the tooltip moved from Oct 10 to Oct 9 with the per-model breakdown, and `aria-describedby` was set.
  - Pointer (dispatched events): calendar hover shows the date and value, and the cell outlines.
  - No console errors.
- Screenshots (local files): /tmp/chart-story/dark-full.jpg, /tmp/chart-story/dark-focus.jpg, /tmp/chart-story/dark-hover-calendar.jpg (light mode, warm palette), /tmp/chart-story/light-warm-top.jpg, /tmp/chart-story/light-warm-bottom.jpg.
- Not verified: real OS focus behaviour in the Electron window, and the phone.

## Risks
- Colour stability is per chart: a key's colour can change if another key in the same chart takes its hash slot first (sorted order). Cross-chart stability holds only while the keys do not collide.
- With more than 8 keys in one chart, colours repeat.
- The tooltip row label is always "Value" on the heat grids. Callers that need units cannot set it yet; add a prop when T13 or T14 need it.
- `formatCompact(999_600)` returns "1000k" (rounding past the unit boundary). It is not used for tick values in practice, and it is not tested.
- Tooltips use a `role="tooltip"` element inside a `role="img"` wrapper. Screen-reader behaviour is not tested; the summary is the main accessible text.
- The chart kit has no legend-to-series highlight and no selection; it is display-only plus hover and focus.

## Recommended Next Step
T11 onward can use `StackedBars`, `CalendarHeatmap`, `MatrixHeatmap`, `HBars`, `SplitBar` and `Sparkline` from `components/Charts.tsx`. Each needs a `summary` string. Pass `formatTokens` or `formatCost` as `format`. Check the colour and label choices against the real data when the Usage page first renders. If a unit label is needed on the heat grids, add an optional `valueLabel` prop there rather than changing callers.

## Facts Learned
- The Models, Projects and Sessions panels are still placeholders (`UsageModels.tsx`, `UsageProjects.tsx`, `UsageSessions.tsx`). Their data is in `UsageReport.models`, `.projects` and `.sessions`, and every other field the node asks for exists: tokens by type, reasoning, estimated and recorded cost, share, cache hit rate, `priced`, `lastAt`, `surface`, `activeMs`, `turns`.

- ATP sessions must open with their identity, as the ATP page does: `threadHandle(cwd, path, title, atp)` in `src/renderer/src/state/atp.ts:145`, where `atp` is `{ role, plan, node }`. The host's `chat.open` treats `atp` as the only source of the ATP skills and prompt (`src/main/session-host.ts:297`); it does not infer it from the path. `SessionRow` carries no plan or node. `userData/atp-threads.json` maps plan to worker paths per node and to the orchestrator path. On this Mac it holds 231 worker paths and 9 orchestrators, all of which exist, and the `atp-sessions` folder has about 250 files, so most ATP rows could be resolved.
- "File no longer exists": the index drops files missing at scan time (`src/main/usage-index.ts:131-136`), but a file removed after the last scan stays in a cached report. The check has to be made at report time, for example with `stat` on the top session rows in `usage-service.ts`.

- No code was written. The node says to report a plan defect before editing, and a per-model thinking split would change the facts' shape, which the design treats as a material divergence (AGENTS.md "Design integrity").
- No decomposition. The other outcomes need the same host changes, and decomposing needs explicit orchestrator authority.

None.

- No typecheck or test run, since nothing changed.

## Risks
- A future per-model thinking split built on per-bucket thinking would multiply hour buckets. The cache is about 3.8 MB against a 4 MB budget (DESIGN.md, Performance budget), so that budget would need revisiting too.

## Recommended Next Step
The orchestrator or user chooses one:
1. **Keep the per-model SplitBar.** Add a thinking level to the facts (a per-bucket level or a separate per-model count), bump `USAGE_FACTS_VERSION` (a cold re-index of about 6 s), and revisit the 4 MB cache budget. Update the DESIGN.md Models note. This is a material facts change and needs approval first.

T16_mobile_usage.title: Add a compact Usage section to the phone's Settings
T16_mobile_usage.instruction:
Goal: the paired phone shows usage too (src/mobile/SettingsScreen.tsx mirrors the desktop sections except Shortcuts).

Steps: add 'usage' to MOBILE_SECTIONS and labels (src/mobile/settings-data.ts); a phone layout with the headline tiles, the daily StackedBars (reuse T10 primitives if they import cleanly into the mobile bundle; check vite.mobile.config.ts and vite.chunks.ts), the models list and the top projects; the range and source filters as a segmented control; progress and empty states. Call usage.get through the host client.
Acceptance: typecheck and tests pass (add settings-data tests); verified through the mobile dev build per docs/REMOTE_VERIFICATION.md or a phone-size browser window (screenshot at iPhone width in the report).
T16_mobile_usage.context: Project: a Usage dashboard in pi-gna's Settings (new section 'Usage', group pi-gna) with in-depth, local-only analytics of how pi and pi-gna were used: tokens by type, estimated cost, models, projects, pi-gna surfaces (chats, card worktrees, ATP workers, subagents), tools, activity over time, agent health and behaviour insights. Data comes only from pi's session JSONL files on this Mac: sessionsDir() in src/main/session-index.ts (~/.pi/agent/sessions, ~1,100 files / 1.6 GB written in the last two weeks) plus pi-gna's userData/atp-sessions (~245 files / 142 MB). Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Principles (lean: no dependency on the pi package, no chart or component library, hand-written SVG + Tailwind; pi owns behaviour, so read pi's files; untrusted content), Settings, Remote access, Verifying the UI; and the '## Usage' section that T01 writes, which is the source of truth for types, metrics and file layout. Code style: flat files in src/main, src/shared, src/renderer/src/components, src/mobile with colocated *.test.ts (vitest); `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` must pass. Nothing leaves the machine: no network for pricing or anything else.

T17_verify_real_surface.title: Verify the whole Usage section on the real app and data
T17_verify_real_surface.instruction:
Goal: end-to-end proof before docs and release.

Steps (follow docs/DESIGN.md 'Verifying the UI'):
1. Run pi-gna from this worktree against the real ~/.pi data (read-only). Cold open: record the index time and confirm the UI stays responsive (scroll, switch sections while indexing). Warm open: under 500 ms.
2. Walk every panel in light, dark and one project theme at normal and narrow widths; keyboard navigation and tooltips; range, source and project filters; opening a session from the Sessions panel; live refresh after a short chat.
3. Compare the headline and model numbers with T09's cross-check summary.
4. Open it on the phone path (or a phone-size window) once.
5. Fix small defects directly (with tests where logic is involved); file anything larger as a card on the Kanban board.

Deliverables: screenshots saved under docs/ (or attached in the report), a short verification log in the report.
Acceptance: no console errors; the numbers agree; no main-thread stalls over ~50 ms during indexing (measure with the Performance panel or timestamps).

T18_docs_changelog.title: Document the Usage dashboard
T18_docs_changelog.instruction:
Goal: users and future agents understand it.

Steps: finalize docs/DESIGN.md '## Usage' (as built: sources, cache file, pricing source and its limits, local time, what counts as pi-gna, the remote exposure); a README feature line; a CHANGELOG entry under the next version; a FAQ or site note that the analytics are computed locally from pi's session files and costs are list-price estimates, not your bill (look for the FAQ in site/ and README). Mention how to reset the index (delete userData/usage-index.json) if you did not add a button.
Acceptance: docs match the code (spot-check names and paths); `pnpm test` still passes.
